Recent relevant work includes a 2026 sequential-recommendation attribution study reporting stronger recency concentration for GRU4Rec and evaluating removal faithfulness, counterfactual stability, and mask-versus-shuffle consistency. Its MovieLens results do not establish the same behavior on Amazon. [Study](https://www.jidmis.org/index.php/jidmis/article/view/2525). The foundational TimeSHAP method provides event-level perturbation attribution and older-prefix pruning, useful for testing whether distant interactions influence predictions; its original experiments concern fraud detection, not recommendation. [TimeSHAP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.00073).

Suggested diagnostic synthesis: within each frozen category model, compare full history against suffix-only history at several suffix lengths, holding the recent suffix, prediction endpoint, target, candidate set, and supervision fixed. Define prefix benefit as rank(suffix-only) − rank(full): positive means helpful older context; negative means harmful. Report paired rank changes, HR@10 gains/losses, and helpful/harmful fractions by original history length and category. Shuffle only the older prefix as a separate order-sensitivity control. These are proposed model-behavior probes, not a published matched-prefix protocol or causal evidence of user intent.

Pair those measurements with update/reset-gate distributions and target-score or target-margin gradient norms versus lag. Gate saturation alone cannot establish forgetting: retention gates near one can preserve information while making gate parameters difficult to learn. [Gating analysis](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/gu20a.html). Large prefix effects despite small local gradients would flag attribution limitations; consistently small effects and decaying gradients would support weak older-context sensitivity. Interpret both as properties of the trained predictor, with sensitivity to perturbation choice.
